sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who is the user, what is the job, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: States the job as getting agreed actions tracked, not just writing summaries
Derives monthly meetings, hours and the on-the-hour peak from the prompt
Names a follow-through metric and an action-item precision target
Lists what is out of scope for v1

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the system as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Separates calendar sync, the meeting bot, transcription, the model and ticket writes into layers
Shows an owner approval step between an action item and a ticket
States one idea that separates what the model drafts from what code and people decide

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: Which inputs does the coworker use, and which one decides who may see the notes?
criteria: Uses the calendar invitee list at meeting time as the access list
Joins only on opt-in and excludes sensitive meeting types by rule
Names a retention limit for audio

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How does audio become a transcript with the right names on it?
criteria: Uses platform speaker events or diarization and justifies the choice
Maps speakers to directory identities through invitee emails
Leaves unresolved speakers unassigned instead of guessing
Estimates transcript size in tokens

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: What is the control flow from transcript to notes and action items?
criteria: Uses a fixed pipeline rather than a free tool-calling agent, with a reason
Decides between one long-context call and map-reduce using token counts
Requires each action item to carry an owner and a quote from the transcript
Adds a verification step that can veto weak action items

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the coworker remember between meetings, and what does it deliberately forget?
criteria: Carries open items forward for recurring meetings without the full old transcript
Gives each memory tier a store and an expiry
Supports deleting a meeting's data on request

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Which tools write to Slack, Docs and the tracker, and under whose identity?
criteria: Creates tickets only when an approval record exists
Writes as the approving user (OAuth) or explains how project permissions are enforced otherwise
Uses an idempotency key so a double click files one ticket
Does not let the model choose where a ticket goes without the owner

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What is the API surface, and how is the 5-minute budget spent?
criteria: Splits meeting-end-to-notes time by stage and the total fits 5 minutes
Acknowledges Slack interactions within 3 s and processes them asynchronously
Verifies webhook signatures and dedupes events
Chooses batch or streaming transcription with a cost or accuracy reason

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What can be cached when every meeting is unique, and what does the system cost?
criteria: Reuses the cached transcript between the notes and action-item calls
Shows per-meeting and monthly model cost with and without caching
Gives an all-in monthly cost including the bot and transcription, within budget

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Where do audio, transcripts and notes live, how big are they, and how is access enforced?
criteria: Sizes audio and transcript storage per month
Enforces retention with lifecycle rules or scheduled purges
Enforces invitee-only access in the data layer, not only in a handler

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does the coworker produce, and how can a reader check it?
criteria: Renders notes from structured data with a fixed template
Links decisions and actions to transcript or recording timestamps
Avoids posting notes to channels with people who were not invitees

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: What enforces consent, access and the no-unapproved-tickets rule if the model or a participant pushes on them?
criteria: Handles consent and notice, including outside or two-party-consent participants
Treats the transcript as untrusted data that cannot trigger actions
Puts access and approval rules in code, not the prompt
Logs who read a transcript

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: What number moves, and how do you know the coworker moved it?
criteria: Gives baseline and target for action items ticketed
Guards the headline with a precision or discard-rate metric
Compares enabled teams against not-yet-enabled teams or another baseline

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what catches each failure?
criteria: Covers the bot failing to join or being stuck in a lobby
Covers an invented or unattributable action item
Covers the tracker being down with an idempotent retry
Covers the on-the-hour burst with a capacity number

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds the labeled eval set first
Ends each step with a measurable number
Puts consent and access before model quality, and ticket writes last
